page: Amazon Web Services g6e.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System, engineered for large-scale graphics, artificial intelligence inference, and high-throughput data processing. The server is powered by AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processors providing 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz. System memory totals 1536.0 GB of DDR4 operating at 3 GHz, delivering 8.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by eight NVIDIA L40S GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture, supplying an aggregate 358 GB of GPU memory. Local high-speed storage comprises 7600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded compute, caching, and acceleration capabilities. In compute workloads, the instance achieves top-tier scores in multi-core stress-ng tests (287028.77) and overall PassMark CPU measurements (114678.67), while showing average throughput in single-core compression benchmarks. Memory subsystems yield over 11800 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and maintain strong uncached throughput above 253 GB/sec. Large language model inference benchmarks reflect top-tier performance across all tested scales, delivering 900.43 tokens per second for prompt processing on 70B parameter models and 5569.58 tokens per second on 7B models. Graphics rendering and simulation capabilities are reinforced by a top-tier Geekbench ray tracing score of 137210.0.

From an infrastructure and cost efficiency perspective, bundling eight high-performance enterprise GPUs, extensive local NVMe storage, and 400 Gbps networking into a single bare-metal-equivalent footprint maximizes resource density. This consolidation minimizes cluster networking overhead and communication latency across distributed nodes. The hardware configuration makes the instance suitable for distributed LLM inference, large-scale ray tracing and rendering pipelines, multi-stream video processing, and in-memory key-value data stores like Redis, which recorded 179.11 million SET operations per second.
description: Amazon Web Services g6e.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for intensive graphics and deep learning workloads. Powered by the AWS Nitro System, it features 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, alongside 1536.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. Acceleration is driven by eight NVIDIA L40S Ada Lovelace GPUs supplying a combined 358 GB of VRAM. The system integrates 7600 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 400 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. In benchmark testing, the platform achieves top-tier results in multi-core stress tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and large language model inference across 7B and 70B parameter configurations, alongside high in-memory Redis throughput exceeding 179 million operations per second. This architecture is designed for multi-GPU model inference, real-time ray tracing, high-density video encoding, and data-intensive analytical pipelines.
